messages.subject: including varuables in modellin the detection probability -- dynamic occupancy in Jags
parts:
Dear modellers,
I'm sure it is a very naive question, but I'm also very naive about the Jags and how to write scripts.
 
 I'm modelling species occupancy using the dynamic occupancy model. I wonder how to include a variable on detection probability and its prior.
I use the below code and an example of jags data (jdata) is attached as a reproducible example.

Your help is really appreciated
###################
cat("
model{
  for(i in 1:nSites) {
    # biological process
    lpsi1[i] <- lpsiInt + bpsi*SST[i]
    psi1[i] <- ilogit(lpsi1[i])
    z[i, 1] ~ dbern(psi1[i])
    for(t in 2:nYears) {
      lphi[i, t-1] <- lphiInt[t-1] + bphi*SST[i]
      phi[i, t-1] <- ilogit(lphi[i, t-1])
      lgam[i, t-1] <- lgamInt[t-1] +  bgam*SST[i]
      gamma[i, t-1] <- ilogit(lgam[i, t-1])
      z[i, t] ~ dbern(z[i, t-1]*phi[i, t-1] +
                        (1 - z[i, t-1])*gamma[i, t-1])
    }
    # detection process
    for(t in 1:nYears) {
     y[i, t] ~ dbin(p[t] * z[i, t], n[i, t])
     
    }
  }
 
  # Priors
  psiInt ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  lpsiInt <- logit(psiInt)
 
  for(t in 1:(nYears-1)) {
    phiInt[t] ~ dbeta(1, 1)
    lphiInt[t] <- logit(phiInt[t])
    gamInt[t] ~ dbeta(1, 1)
    lgamInt[t] <- logit(gamInt[t])
  }
 
  for(t in 1:nYears) {
    p[t] ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  }
 
  bpsi ~ dunif(0,1)
  bphi ~ dunif(0,1)
  bgam ~ dunif(0,1)
 
 
 
  # Derived variable
  for(t in 1:nYears) {
    N[t] <- sum(z[,t]) # no. sites occupied for each year
  }
}", fill=TRUE, file="dynoccSST.text")

messages.subject: AW: including varuables in modellin the detection probability -- dynamic occupancy in Jags
parts:
Dear Alaa,

 

and what exactly is your question ?

 

Basically, in your model adding a covariate on detection prob p will produce the form of a logistic regression exactly as for the models on psi1, gamma and phi on your model. That is,  you can add a covariate with as many values as you have years t, in your formulation of the model. And then you write something like this in the likelihood:

 

  for(t in 1:nYears) {
   p[t] <- ilogit(lp[t])

   lp[t] <- alpha.lp + beta.lp * cov[t]
  }

 

As for priors, I like to give a U(0,1) on the intercept of a logistic regression in the inverse-link scale. That is:

 

alpha.lp <- logit(mean.p)

mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)

 

Then, for the coefficient beta, this is a real number that may a priori be either positive or negative. Hence, I’d give a prior like one of these:

 

beta.lp ~ dunif(-5, 5)         or                                        

beta.lp ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)                                                      

 

I note that in your code below, I don’t think that the priors for the covariates on the other parameters make sense, since you constrain them to live on 0 to 1. I’d choose some prior for them as what I suggest here for the covariate in a model for p.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

Dear Marc,

Thanks a million for your prompt reply.
This was exactly what i'm looking for. I was confused with the detection formula but you made it clear.
Thanks also for your suggestion to not to constrain the prior of the other covariates. It did improve the model.

Cheers,  Alaa
